title: Some Antidepressants May Work Better Than Others Long Term - Nautilus
author: Lauren Cortis
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthSome Antidepressants May Work Better Than Others Long TermBut does that mean these are the best antidepressants?LCJJBy Lauren Cortis and Jack Janetzki11:00 AM CST on November 13, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleAnew review has found some antidepressants may be more effective than others at helping people reduce the severity of their symptoms of depression over the long term.Powered By 1058.2K 20ShareNextStayThe research, published in The Lancet Psychiatry, found people taking escitalopram (commonly sold as Lexapro), duloxetine (Cymbalta) and agomelatine (Valdoxan) were more likely to report improved symptoms over the long term than those taking fluoxetine (Prozac). For those taking Lexapro and Cymbalta, they were also more likely to stay on their medications.But does that mean these are the best antidepressants?Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
